STEP 1 - Vessel type: square flat plate (white, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are 20-30 cm; this one looks medium-large, so about 26 cm.
b) Reference: the plate is roughly 2.5 olives' worth... better: the chickpeas are about 1.0-1.2 cm each and the plate spans about 22-24 chickpeas across the rim region; the artichoke halves are about 8-9 cm long and roughly 2.5-3 lengths fit across the width (~24 cm). Both cues agree on about 24 cm.
Final width = 24 cm, square, area = 576 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:
- Chickpeas: about 45 visible, plus a few hidden, say 50 in total. Chickpea is about 0.3 g each cooked, so roughly 15-20 g. Estimate 40 g including the small cluster in the upper right (cooked chickpeas, ~1.0 cm each, wet and piled 1-2 deep). Using footprint: ~10% of area (58 cm²) x 1 cm thickness x 0.6 density ≈ 35 g. Take 40 g.
- Kalamata-style olives: about 9 visible, pit-in, each about 3.5-4 g. Count 9 x 4 g = 36 g.
- Artichoke hearts (quartered/halved, three to four pieces): footprint about 15% (86 cm²) x 1.5 cm average x 0.8 density ≈ 100 g. Use 110 g.
- Chicken or white fish-like flaked meat (the crumbly white pile, bottom left): footprint about 12% (69 cm²) x 1.5 cm average x 1.0 density ≈ 100 g. Note: appears to be shredded chicken or tuna-like flakes; take 100 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer clearly visible beyond the items; the plate is largely flat, so no extra layer added.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Chickpeas, cooked: 164 kcal/100 g
- Olives, cured: 150 kcal/100 g
- Artichoke hearts, canned in water/brine: 50 kcal/100 g
- Shredded chicken/white meat: 165 kcal/100 g

Totals: chickpeas 66 kcal, olives 54 kcal, artichoke 55 kcal, meat 165 kcal. Total ≈ 340 kcal from about 286 g.
